intro: Four small answers about time, and adverbs in -mente.
p.aún.nota: With an accent, aún usually means todavía.
p.aun.nota: Without an accent, aun usually means incluso; aún with an accent means still/yet.
b1.titulo: Has it happened, does it go on
b1.texto:
In these patterns, **ya** says a change has happened: **ya** he terminado. **Ya no** says something has stopped: **ya no** vivo allí.

**Todavía** (or **aún**) says something continues: **todavía** vivo allí. **Todavía no** (or **aún no**) says it has not happened yet: **todavía no** he comido.

They answer each other: — ¿**Ya** has comido? — **Todavía no**. / — ¿**Todavía** trabajas allí? — **Ya no**.

**Ya voy** means I'm coming. With an accent, **aún** means still/yet; without one, **aun** usually means even.

Adverbs in **-mente** are built on the feminine adjective: rápida → **rápidamente**, fácil → **fácilmente**. The written accent stays. Good and bad have their own adverbs: habla **bien**, canta **mal**.
b3.f2: Do you still work at the hospital?
b3.f3: No, I don't work there any more. Now I only study.
b3.f4: At last! Now we can go.
b5.pregunta: Complete: I don't live there any more.
b6.pregunta: Complete with todavía: — Have you finished? — No, ___ no.
b6.o1.refuerzo: Ya no would mean no longer.
b7.pregunta: How do you make an adverb from «rápido»?
b7.o0.refuerzo: Feminine form plus -mente, and the accent stays.
b8.o2.explicacion: That would be ya no voy.
b9.traduccion: I don't work at the hospital any more.
b10.texto:
**The app cannot check this part.** For the writing, please use pen and paper. For the speaking, say it out loud and, if you can, practise with a native speaker or a teacher who can correct you.

**Write (60–80 words).** Write a to-do list for a trip and mark each thing: Ya he…, todavía no he…

**Speak (about 1 minute).** Say aloud what you have already done today and what you have not done yet.
